# Factory readiness and evidence-driven delivery

## Load only what is needed

1. Read repository AGENTS and Copilot instructions; preserve user changes and
   frozen acceptance/contract/regression suites.
2. Read [verified baseline](../../../docs/READINESS-2026-09-12.md) and
   [scope, decisions and execution plan](../../../docs/DELIVERY-PLAN.md).
3. Inspect current status and the requested work package. Read only relevant
   spec sections and modules; the old audit is a starting point, not live truth.
4. Keep a small package ledger: baseline/digests, tests, results, review,
   spend, blockers and next action. Update repository memory with verified
   reusable lessons, not transcripts or secrets.

## Stable rules

- Workspace root is a wrapper; factory/payments are separate Git repositories.
  SDK/infra were only folders at the audit; check before any Git action.
- On Windows use each repository's existing virtual environment. The editor may
  select the factory interpreter for payments; it lacks target dependencies.
  Put Git Bash ahead of System32/WSL Bash for the subprocess test fixtures.
- Follow configured Python/container tools first. The user approved Podman for
  this workspace's disposable tests; container settings may still say Docker.
- No commit, push, merge, cloud/production destination or unbounded spending by
  implication. $20 was the aggregate simulation ceiling, not recurring authority.
- Current quorum decision: one person available; sensitive production waits for
  a second distinct human. AI or two accounts of one person cannot satisfy it.
- TDD: reproduce first, implement minimally, preserve frozen tests, verify
  focused/full tests/types/lint/coverage/scans and independent review. Never
  weaken evidence or repair the same failure speculatively more than twice.
- Different model instances/provider labels do not prove family independence.
  Missing reviewer is unavailable, not a rejection or an approval.

## Doer/reviewer standard

Use [ARP-1](../../../docs/AGENT-REVIEW-POLICY.md) for every semantic artifact in
agentic workflows run or generated by the factory. Pin criteria and relevant C4/
interface/test evidence; doer produces, another model reviews, doer fixes or
rebuts with evidence, reviewer validates closure. Minimum two genuine completed
review passes, recommended maximum three, finite parent budgets and persisted
failure counters. Two passes do not require invented edits or two clean votes
on obsolete content. Optional preferences do not drive repairs; mandatory gaps
block regardless of severity. No self-review, recursive reviewer loops or
unreviewed final repair. Stop on repeated real failure or unavailable capacity;
do not claim model-family independence without verified model identities.

This is documented direction pending A00/A05–A07 implementation. Two planning
subagent reviews are not proof of runtime enforcement or cross-family qualification.

## Audit workflow

1. Pin local/remote SHAs, branch, dirty paths and tool versions. Do not fetch or
   mutate provider state unless authorized. Reconcile historical claims with
   current evidence; invisible org repos remain unknown, not absent.
2. Separate implemented functionality, schema/protocol scaffolding, security
   defects, product gaps and administrative/provider blockers.
3. Run existing baseline tests before new regressions. Factory: Ruff, strict
   mypy, pytest, acceptance; payments: its own equivalent gates. SDK: locked
   install/build and genuine test command without no-tests bypass. Infra:
   format/init-without-backend/validate; never apply by implication.
4. Use [core probes](./scripts/readiness_probes.py) with explicit pytest and
   [workflow probes](./scripts/workflow_probes.mjs) with Node's built-in test
   runner. They intentionally FAILED on the audited scaffold. They are opt-in
   regressions, not baseline passes, xfails or proof of GitHub enforcement.
5. For runtime smoke use an owned resource-limited Jaeger container with a
   unique label/name and loopback ports. From payments' cwd/venv execute
   [telemetry smoke](./scripts/telemetry_smoke.py) with a unique synthetic
   `--work-item-id`, port arguments and `--mode emit`. Run `--mode verify`
   independently once receipt is available. Export flush is not indexed receipt.
   Do not introduce sleeps or hide indexing failures by calling emission PASS.
6. Distinguish ASGI health requests/direct synthetic spans from actual refund
   business behavior, and both from a full factory-run story. Verify the receiver
   and work-item tags; capture exact evidence before cleanup.
7. Stop/remove only resources created by this run; preserve existing containers,
   images and volumes. No real financial/claims side effects or customer data.
8. Report actual command exits/counts. Read truncated-output artifacts; an empty
   or contradictory execution summary is not proof. Inspect safe raw GitHub
   responses when a filter returns nothing. Never print secret values.

## Execute a saved pass

Use the plan's dependency order and earliest incomplete ledger entry. Work
through all independent, authorized packages without asking for each file edit.
New frozen contracts need their independent authoring/approval lane. Required
provider/model/cloud tests must actually run before qualification; fakes only
prove local contracts. Persist blocked cells and one consolidated prerequisite
request. A resumable pass is not a guarantee that an entire SaaS product finishes
in one context window.

## Output

Summarize: readiness verdict; concrete verified results and reproduced failures;
completed versus remaining packages; consequential/admin blockers; spend and
cleanup; exact next action. Link the saved evidence/plan rather than pasting the
specification or whole repository. Never equate green unit tests with delivery.
